# Independent audit: large response atoms and minimal circuits

Audited `candidate 44be00e92663306c`.
Result: PASS. No repair requested.

The hinge [N.w-c]_+ is an actual nonnegative convex physical field, and
the outward kernel equals1 wherever that hinge is positive. Properness
in the source inball makes its boundary integral strictly positive. The
resulting efficiency inequality is pointwise before integration; it does
not substitute volume capture for boundary capture.

Summing k separately normalized fields has total boundary integral k.
All cross captures and the covariance-quadratic terms are nonnegative.
The only adverse width term is bounded by h S_max k/(2M), which gives the
stated simultaneous group loss. The choice of menus precedes separation,
so no separator is silently reused after changing menus.

For completeness, the minimal-circuit linear algebra also checks. Put
v_j=S_j u_j and let a positive extreme probability satisfy sum nu_j v_j=0.
The row of ones is independent of the rows of the v matrix: otherwise
multiplying a proposed relation by nu would give1=0. Extremality on k
positive atoms therefore implies rank(v)=k-1. Its nullspace is generated
by the positive balance vector. A repeated/parallel pair or an antipodal
pair in a larger menu would give another dependence on a proper subset.
Rank1 is exactly a two-atom antipodal circuit, with some RESPONSE atom
at least1/2. This proves the claimed Gamma_d hinge payment independently
of base tilts. It does not assert that higher-rank menus have a large atom.
